title: Caramelized White Chocolate and Macadamia Nut Cookies
story: White chocolate out of the bag is fine. Caramelized white chocolate, which takes about 40 minutes of occasionally stirring it in the oven, tastes closer to butterscotch than anything you'd normally call white chocolate. Worth knowing about. The sea salt on top is doing more work than it gets credit for.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
½ cup macadamia nuts, roughly chopped
½ cup white chocolate, roughly chopped

steps.text: In a medium bowl, whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, and ½ tsp fine salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter, ½ cup granulated sugar, and ½ cup packed brown sugar together until light and creamy, about 2–3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look noticeably paler and fluffy, not grainy or dense — this step builds the cookie's lift and texture.

steps.text: Beat in 1 large egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract until fully combined and smooth.
Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain — overmixing toughens the cookie.
Fold in ½ cup roughly chopped macadamia nuts and ½ cup roughly chopped white chocolate.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.
Sprinkle each cookie with a small pinch of flaky sea salt before they go in the oven.

steps.donenessCue: Edges are golden brown and centers look just barely set — they'll firm up as they cool. Pull them when they still look slightly underdone in the middle; overbaked is a much bigger risk here than underbaked.

steps.text: Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. They're fragile straight from the oven.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: To actually caramelize the white chocolate: spread it on a parchment-lined pan and bake at 250°F (120°C), stirring every 10 minutes for 30–40 minutes, until deep golden and caramel-scented. Cool completely before chopping and folding in — this is where the name really earns itself.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes before baking. The cookies will spread less and the brown sugar flavor deepens noticeably.
Toast the macadamia nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes before chopping. Cool completely before folding in.
Add ½ tsp almond extract alongside the vanilla — it plays quietly with the white chocolate without announcing itself.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. To freeze: roll into balls, freeze on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen at 350°F, adding 2–3 minutes to the bake time.
